entities.name: Louis de Beaupoil de Saint-Aulaire
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Louis-Clair de Beaupoil, comte de Saint-Aulaire (died 1854), emerged as a prominent French statesman and diplomat during the turbulent transition from the Bourbon Restoration to the July Monarchy, serving as a pivotal figure in shaping France's domestic and foreign policy. Born into an ancient noble family in Périgord, Saint-Aulaire navigated the complex political landscape of early 19th-century France, leveraging his aristocratic lineage and liberal convictions to secure influential positions. His career spanned significant diplomatic postings in Rome and London, alongside a critical role in the French Chamber of Peers, making him a key architect of the Orleanist regime's international standing and internal stability.

Saint-Aulaire's political ascent accelerated following the July Revolution of 1830, which saw the establishment of the liberal July Monarchy under King Louis-Philippe I. From 1831 to 1832, he served as the French Ambassador to the Holy See, skillfully negotiating the intricate relationship between the new, secular-leaning French government and the Papacy during a period of considerable anti-clerical sentiment in France. Subsequently, he was appointed Ambassador to the United Kingdom from 1833 to 1841, where he worked tirelessly to strengthen the Anglo-French Entente, a cornerstone of Louis-Philippe's foreign policy aimed at maintaining European peace and containing more radical forces. His diplomatic tenure in London was crucial in managing crises such as the Oriental Question and fostering commercial ties, demonstrating a pragmatic approach to international relations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Louis de Beaupoil de Saint-Aulaire was a significant figure in French 19th-century politics and diplomacy, playing a crucial role in stabilizing the July Monarchy through his ambassadorships in Rome and London, and his leadership in the Chamber of Peers. His efforts contributed to strengthening Anglo-French relations and managing complex European political issues during his era.
